topic: Water-wrinkled fingers: nerve-driven vasoconstriction, nerve test, grip theory
hook: Why do your fingers wrinkle in water?

design.follow_line: One surprising body fact every day

caption:
Ten minutes in the bath and your fingertips look like raisins. Most people think it's water soaking into the skin. In fact, your nerves tell the blood vessels under your fingertips to tighten. The skin then pulls into folds.

The proof: fingers with cut nerves stay smooth in water. That's why doctors can use water-wrinkling as a simple test for nerve damage. Why we evolved it is still debated. One idea is better grip on wet things, but studies disagree.

Send this to someone who stays in the shower way too long. Did you know your nerves did this?
